title: Inference plan selector drift: rapid safeguard, customer mitigations, and durable fix
creator: Anika Rao
description: Several customers reported increased time-to-first-token (TTFT) and decreased tokens/sec across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters after a model-profile sync rolled out a new inference-plan scoring heuristic. The symptom profile: first-token latency regressed for mixed short/long sessions and tokens/sec dropped during 99th-percentile bursts. Impacted customers included a mid-market payments customer on Dedicated and two Hosted PLG customers with multi-tenant fanout patterns. This ticket contains the triage timeline, immediate mitigations, verification steps, and follow-up action items for a durable fix.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Anika Rao: Triage started after on-call alert and two customer escalations (payments-corp, research-ai). Initial hypothesis: new plan-scoring heuristic favors a quantized kernel variant that increases latency under heterogeneous session lengths.

2026-03-01 - Marcus Chen: Reproduced locally using customer trace replay (s3://replay/2026-03-01/payments-corp). Observed kernel contention on worker GPUs and repeated KV cache evictions when mixed short and long requests interleave.

2026-03-02 - Marcus Chen: Emergency mitigation deployed: disabled the new plan scoring flag in Hosted regions us-east-1 and eu-west-1; triggered controlled rollback for Dedicated customer pools that reported the highest regressions.
2026-03-02 - SRE (Priya Kumar): Applied regional traffic steering to move affected requests to warm Dedicated pools for the payments customer. This reduced 95/99 TTFT by ~40% within 12 minutes.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Chen: Hotpatch (PR #4713) introduced a short-term guardrail: if model seq-dist variance > threshold, fall back to stable kernel selection. Patch reverted the heuristic decision for mixed-context batches.

2026-03-03 - QA (Diego Morales): Validated hotpatch against the replay corpus and synthetic fanout scenarios. No functional regressions found; load tests show tokens/sec recovered to baseline on replicas with weight > 0.8.
2026-03-04 - Customer Success (Lina Park): Payments customer confirmed service restoration; logged an incident call and asked for a postmortem and SLA credit estimate.

2026-03-04 - Marcus Chen: Began work on durable fix: update scoring to consider per-model sequence-length distribution, tenancy-local KV pressure, and per-worker affinity metrics. Added new telemetry for plan-selection decisions.
2026-03-05 - Anika Rao: Drafted post-incident action items and a canary plan for runtime-2.3 that gates the new scoring behind additional safety metrics.

2026-03-05 - Marcus Chen: Submitted PRs and config change proposals: PR #4720 (durable scoring logic), PR #4721 (telemetry counters and tracing tags), and rollout runbook updates at confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INFR-204212.
2026-03-05 - SRE (Priya Kumar): Added Datadog dashboards (dd://dash/infra/plan-selector) and alert rules to detect divergence between expected and actual kernel latency per model.

Next steps: Merge durable fix after code review, run 2-hour canary against low-traffic region, add unit/integration tests to prevent heuristic regressions, and schedule postmortem with CS and impacted customers.
